Article Title: 143-year-old Pittsburgh paint company finds its biggest boom as Microsoft, Google, Amazon build AI data centres; gray paint sales to data centres set to triple; VP says: “I’ve never seen a…
Article Text:
Fans that are part of a cooling system are seen on the roof of a data center, Monday, April 27, 2026, in Hillsboro, Ore. (AP Photo/Jenny Kane)

Data centre paint sales are outrunning PPG's overall growth

Steelguard 951 swells into a crust that keeps fire away from steel

PPG, a 143-year-old Pittsburgh company that started out making glass, has found an unlikely growth engine in AI data centres. The firm expects its paint sales to data centres to triple this year from last year, The New York Times reported. The coatings are mostly gray and they do a serious job, shielding steel from fire, rust and static electricity inside the huge facilities that Microsoft, Google, Amazon and other tech giants are racing to build. "I've never seen a boom as big as this," said Jenn Solcz, PPG's vice president of protective and marine coatings for the Americas.The surge stands out against the rest of the business. PPG's total sales rose 7% to $4.5 billion in the most recent quarter, and data centres still make up only a low-single-digit share of sales in two parts of the company, executives told the Times. Amy Ericson, a PPG senior vice president, expects data centres to grow "multiple times" faster than other infrastructure markets.Rival Sherwin-Williams is seeing a similar pull. Its chief executive, Heidi Petz, said in July that its protective and marine sales rose by a midteens percentage from a year earlier, helped by data centre construction.Speed is a big part of the pitch. Data centres go up in about a third of the time a typical infrastructure project takes, Solcz said, so PPG built one team for the tech giants and another that works with architects and builders before construction begins.The aim is to get its coatings written into a project's approved materials list early.In April, PPG rolled out a data centre package at a trade show in Washington. It covers steel fireproofing, rust-resistant primers, anti-static flooring and coatings that block electrical interference between machines. The company also makes coatings for more than 75 data centre parts, including security camera housings and cooling equipment.The flagship product is Steelguard 951. At PPG's test facility near Pittsburgh, researchers aimed torches at coated steel panels inside a concrete building called "the bunker." Paul Fenton, a PPG chemist, held up one panel where a 1 mm layer of paint had swollen into a black crust almost 10 mm tall. Trapped air keeps the steel cool, he said, "just like a toasted marshmallow."The coating can protect steel for up to four hours, which gives people time to get out. Fires at data centres can start at backup generators, batteries or nearby power plants.Looks barely matter. PPG's shades are named light gray, gray and dark gray, and data centres are filled with machines, not people. Pipes are the exception, with blue for chilled water and red for sprinklers. Matthew Giddings of real estate firm JLL said paint can cost $3 million to $8 million for one building, a sliver of construction costs.There are bumps ahead. Some projects are waiting on power, transformer shortages have stretched timelines, and local opposition is growing. Ericson said the backlash is for tech companies and utilities to handle.PPG began in 1883 as the Pittsburgh Plate Glass Company. In 2024, it sold its US and Canadian paint-store business, including the Glidden brand, and now mostly serves businesses, coating cars, aircraft and beverage cans.
Article Summary: Pittsburgh-based PPG has found an unlikely growth engine in AI data centres. The firm expects its paint sales to data centres to triple this year from last year. PPG's total sales rose 7% to $4.5 billion in the most recent quarter.

Article Title: Apple’s India story is getting bigger: Record iPhone upgrades, Mac sales and services revenue
Article Text:
FILE - The Apple logo is illuminated at a store in Munich, Germany, April 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Matthias Schrader, File)

The iPhone still brings customers back to Apple in India and perhaps is the gateway to the hallowed ecosystem from Cupertino. The September quarter offered a glimpse of what else they might buy once they’re there. Apple posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in the country, with Macs and services also setting all-time India records. At the same time, CEO John Ternus said more people in India upgraded their iPhones than in any previous September quarter.Put those numbers together and there’s a more interesting story than another strong quarter for the iPhone. Apple has three ways to grow in India: sell an existing customer their next iPhone, persuade them to consider a Mac when they need a laptop, and earn from services in the years between those purchases. The earnings call showed strength in all three. It didn’t tell us how often the same customer was doing all three.The Mac record is particularly interesting because it works in both directions. An iPhone owner shopping for a laptop may give the MacBook Neo a look because it costs less than other MacBooks and works with a phone they already own. For someone replacing a Windows laptop who has never owned an Apple device, the Neo could be their first purchase from the company.Either would widen Apple’s reach in India in a way that selling a new Mac to someone replacing an old one wouldn’t.CFO Kevan Parekh credited the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro for global Mac revenue growth of 24% to $10.8 billion. Apple didn’t say which models drove the India record or how many buyers were new to the Mac. That is the detail to watch: a strong quarter for the Pro and a quarter in which the Neo wins over first-time Mac buyers can both produce record revenue, but only one tells you that Apple is reaching people who might never have considered a Mac.Services add another dimension. Someone can keep the same iPhone for years and still pay Apple every month for iCloud storage or spend money on the App Store. Globally, services brought in $31.6 billion, up 10% and more than a quarter of Apple’s $114.5 billion in quarterly revenue. Apple hasn’t said how close India is to that mix, or whether its local record came from more paying customers, higher spending by existing users or other sources of revenue.For years, a good quarter for Apple in India was easiest to read through the iPhone. That’s still where much of the attention will go. But the Mac and services records give us two more things to watch: whether Apple is becoming a serious option when Indians shop for a laptop, and what customers are willing to pay for after they’ve bought the device.
Article Summary: Apple posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in the country, with Macs and services also setting all-time India records. Apple has three ways to grow in India: sell an existing customer their next iPhone, persuade them to consider a Mac when they need a laptop, and earn from services in the years between those purchases.

Article Title: As JP Morgan and Charles Schwab say 'not allowed' to AI agents; Accenture warns: You are risking…
Article Text:
Consumers open to AI, but want control

Security concerns real, but not the whole story

'We've seen this movie before'

Banks still have a major role to play

Agentic flooding: an infrastructure challenge

Blocking AI agents may not work in the long run

As JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab and several major retailers move to keep personal AI agents out of their systems, consulting firm Accenture is warning that the strategy may backfire. According to a report by CNBC, Michael Abbott, Accenture's global banking lead, has warned that organisations risk falling behind if they focus on blocking AI agents instead of creating secure ways for them to interact with customers' accounts. “If customers explicitly authorize an AI agent to act on their behalf, that’s ultimately an extension of customer choice,” he said. The more important question, in his view, is not whether institutions can block agents but whether they can create a secure and trusted way for them to engage.As per the CNBC report, Abbott mentioned that the consumers are becoming open to using AI-powered tools to manage their financial activities, and the banks should view this as an opportunity rather than a threat. As per the Accenture Research report, around 64% of consumers are willing to use a GPT-like financial assistant via a generative AI platform or digital wallet and 71% would welcome an AI assistant integrated into their primary mobile banking app."If customers explicitly authorise an AI agent to act on their behalf, that's ultimately an extension of customer choice," Abbott said. He added that the more important issue for institutions is creating secure and trusted mechanisms for AI agents to engage with banking systems rather than attempting to block them outright.Asked to distinguish genuine security worries from companies protecting profits, Abbott said both can be true at once. He acknowledged “very real concerns around fraud, identity verification, liability and consumer protection,” adding that banks’ responsibility to safeguard customer assets and data does not disappear because an AI agent is involved. At the same time, he noted, consumers have historically benefited from technologies that improve transparency and make it easier to compare options.Drawing parallels with previous technology shifts, Abbott said the industry has experienced similar concerns during the rise of online banking, mobile banking and digital wallets. Consumers ultimately gravitated towards technologies that reduced friction and saved time, he noted."We've seen this movie before," Abbott said, arguing that institutions that adapt to changing customer behaviour typically emerge stronger than those that resist technological change. According to Abbott, the winners are usually the organisations that find safe ways to participate in new digital trends rather than trying to prevent them.Even as customer interactions increasingly move beyond bank-owned platforms and applications, Abbott believes financial institutions can remain central to the customer experience. He said banks have an opportunity to become trusted providers of data, intelligence and transaction execution for AI agents. As customers rely more on AI tools to make financial decisions, banks need to ensure they are present at critical decision-making moments, even if the customer is interacting through a third-party interface.On fears that millions of agents could overwhelm websites and customer-service systems, Abbott called it a possibility rather than a crisis. “I see it more as an infrastructure challenge than an existential threat,” he said, noting that most digital systems were designed for human interactions, while one person might soon have multiple agents continuously monitoring rates and comparing products. The answer, he said, is not to block agents but “to build the next generation of infrastructure that can authenticate trusted agents, verify permissions, manage identity and support machine-to-machine interactions efficiently. ” That, he added, is nothing new for banks: customers once interacted with them a couple of times a month and now do so nearly daily through mobile. “AI agents are just the next evolution. The organizations that prepare for that reality will be better positioned than those that try to prevent it.”Abbott also cautioned that AI-driven interactions could eventually operate at a scale far beyond what today's digital systems were designed to handle. Instead of blocking agents, organisations should focus on building infrastructure capable of authenticating trusted AI systems, verifying permissions and managing secure machine-to-machine interactions."AI agents are just the next evolution," Abbott said. "The organisations that prepare for that reality will be better positioned than those that try to prevent it."His comments come amid a broader debate across the financial services industry over how AI agents should interact with customer accounts. While some companies are restricting access because of security concerns, Accenture's view suggests that consumer demand and technological evolution may make resistance increasingly difficult over the long term.
Article Summary: Accenture's global banking lead Michael Abbott has warned that organisations risk falling behind if they focus on blocking AI agents. He added that the more important issue for institutions is creating secure and trusted mechanisms for AI agents to engage with banking systems rather than attempting to block them outright.

Article Title: Shark Tank judge Anupam Mittal questions ESOP tax rules; says employees are punished for ownership
Article Text:
Here’s what Anupam Mittal said

Shark Tank judge and Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal has questioned the country’s tax rules for Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs), saying employees are taxed heavily when they exercise their stock options and become shareholders. In a post on LinkedIn, Anupam Mittal argued that the tax system should encourage employee ownership instead of making it costly, especially as startups look to attract talent and create wealth. For those unaware, ESOPs allow employees to buy shares in a company at a fixed price, often giving them a chance to benefit as the business grows. However, when employees exercise their options, the difference between the purchase price and the market value of the shares is generally taxed as a salary perquisite at their applicable income tax rate.Anupam Mittal’s comments also come amid a recent Bengaluru Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) ruling involving a Flipkart employee. The tribunal held that proceeds from the company’s repurchase of vested but unexercised ESOPs could be taxed as long-term capital gains (LTCG), rather than as salary perquisites. However, the tax treatment depends on the structure and circumstances of the transaction.Sharing his views on X, Mittal wrote:“Why does India punish employee ownership?We keep telling employees - Think like an owner.Then we tax them for becoming one 🤷🏻Say you get ESOPs at ₹10.You exercise when the share is worth ₹100. That ₹90 appreciation can be taxed as a perquisite at your marginal rate, potentially ~40%.Why should emp wealth be treated less favourably than long-term wealth created by public or private investors?ESOPs aren’t compensation alone.They are how startups turn employees into owners, align incentives and spread wealth creation beyond founders and investors.If we believe India needs more startups, more employment generation & more wealth creation....then perhaps we should encourage ESOP ownership, not something we need tax lawyers for.Cheat code - If you can get your co to buy back your ESOPS instead of exercising them, recent case law suggests the gain qualifies for LTCG”
Article Summary: Shark Tank judge and Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal questioned the country’s tax rules for Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs) He said employees are taxed heavily when they exercise their stock options and become shareholders. Mittal argued that the tax system should encourage employee ownership.

Article Title: Zomato launches Host Mode, lets users hide menu prices from guests: Here’s how it works
Article Text:
Designed to make hosting more comfortable

How Host Mode works

Feature inspired by customer feedback

Food delivery platform Zomato has launched a new feature called Host Mode, aimed at making group food ordering more comfortable by hiding menu prices from guests while allowing hosts to retain control over the final bill. The new feature, which is now available to users across India, enables guests to browse restaurant menus and add dishes to the cart without seeing the cost of individual items. Hosts can later review the complete bill and place the order after authenticating with a passcode, fingerprint, or face lock.According to Zomato, the feature addresses a common social situation where guests often hesitate to order their preferred dishes when someone else is paying. The company said many diners tend to choose less expensive items or leave the decision to the host, while hosts typically want their guests to order freely without worrying about the cost.With Host Mode enabled, prices are removed from restaurant menus and the cart, allowing guests to focus solely on choosing what they would like to eat. The total bill remains hidden until the host decides to exit the mode and review the order.The company said the feature is particularly relevant during the festive season, when families and friends frequently gather and order food together.Users can activate the feature by tapping the Host Mode option available on the app's home screen, restaurant menu pages, or through the preferences section in their profile.Once enabled, prices disappear across menus and the cart, and guests can add items without seeing any pricing information. When the order is ready, the host can tap the option to exit Host Mode, authenticate using biometric verification or device security credentials, and view the complete bill, including any discounts or savings, before placing the order.Zomato said only the host can reveal the bill, ensuring that pricing details remain private throughout the ordering process.The company revealed that Host Mode originated from a suggestion shared by a Zomato customer on social media. According to Zomato, the idea was developed and rolled out on the app within 72 hours, with the goal of making social hosting and food ordering more seamless for customers. The launch adds to Zomato's ongoing efforts to introduce features aimed at improving user experience on its food delivery platform, particularly around social and group ordering occasions.
Article Summary: Zomato has launched a new feature called Host Mode, aimed at making group food ordering more comfortable by hiding menu prices. The new feature, which is now available to users across India, enables guests to browse restaurant menus and add dishes to the cart without seeing the cost of individual items.

Article Title: Google launches Dreambeans AI app to India, brings personalised story collections in 14 languages
Article Text:
What is Google’s Dreambeans app

Uses data from Google's apps

Available in 14 Indian languages

Google has announced that its experimental AI-powered app—Dreambeans is now available in India. The Dreambeans app is available for all the users above 18 years of age across the country. The tech giant has also revealed that the app is developed by Google Labs and is available on both Android and iOS operating systems. “Starting today, Dreambeans, an experimental app from Google Labs that creates personalized daily story collections, is expanding to people in India (18+),” said Google in a blog post.As per Google, Dreambeans is designed to connect you with what matters without the endless scroll. The app can help users create personalised daily story collections on the basis of their interests and activities. “Dreambeans is designed to connect you with what matters without the endless scroll. This could be everything from places to explore, new arts & crafts, or a reminder of upcoming local events. You can dive deeper into any story to learn more, bookmark for later, or easily share with others to spark inspiration,” added Google.Google says that the app is designed to help people discover information that matters to them without having to endlessly scroll through feeds and content streams.Google said Dreambeans generates its personalised content using information from selected Google services that users choose to connect. These include Google Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Google Photos, Google Search and YouTube. The company added that user feedback will help improve the quality and relevance of stories generated by the app over time“Dreambeans brews your stories using information from the Google apps you select, including Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube. Share your feedback to make your stories even better over time,” said Google.As part of its India rollout, Dreambeans is launching with support for 14 languages. These include Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Tamil, Urdu, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Punjabi, Assamese and Nepali, among others. Google said the app is available for download starting today through both the Google Play Store and Apple's App Store
Article Summary: Google has announced that its experimental AI-powered app—Dreambeans is now available in India. The Dreambeans app is available for all the users above 18 years of age across the country. The tech giant has also revealed that the app is developed by Google Labs.

Article Title: Why basic phones are holding on in the age of AI smartphones
Article Text:
कंपनी 8 अक्टूबर से शुरू हो रही फ्लिपकार्ट बिग बिलियन डेज सेल में स्मार्टफोन को बेचेगी।

New Delhi: India’s basic phone is refusing to hang up. As rising smartphone prices put upgrades beyond some buyers’ budgets, feature-phone manufacturers are adding digital payments and other services to devices whose biggest attractions remain affordability, battery life and simplicity. The pressure on smartphone affordability has intensified since September. Counterpoint Research’s October 23 report showed shipments below Rs 20,000 falling 47% year-on-year in July–September, partly because price increases pushed models into higher bands. Overall smartphone shipments declined 20%. That does not establish a shift towards feature phones, but it provides a sharper backdrop to why their users may postpone upgrading.Arijeet Talapatra, CEO of itel India, Transsion Holdings, described the feature-phone category as increasingly driven by replacement demand. Affordability remains the biggest draw, alongside durability, multi-day battery life and ease of use.“Feature phones continue to serve a distinct and practical need: they offer reliable, essential connectivity at a price and level of simplicity that smartphones cannot always replicate,” he said.Ravi Kunwar, vice-president and CEO, HMD India and APAC, estimated that around 200 million people still use 2G feature phones. That represents an existing user base, rather than annual handset sales.“Consumers are looking for better connectivity and more features, but that does not always mean they want to move to a smartphone,” Kunwar said.Digital payments are expanding what compatible basic handsets can do. PhonePe announced its UPI 123Pay service on August 31, using an SMS-based system that does not require mobile internet. Its current terms allow transfers, merchant payments and QR scanning on camera-equipped feature phones, with one bank account enabled at a time.At launch, PhonePe named Nokia, HMD, Lava and itel as handset partners. It also announced an activation helpline supporting English and 12 Indian languages. Bill payments, recharges and Aadhaar-based onboarding were described as forthcoming; their rollout needs confirmation before being presented as available.More capabilities, however, have not produced consistent shipment growth. CMR’s April–June 2026 data showed 2G feature-phone shipments rising 5% year-on-year while 4G models declined 43%. Itel held 38% of the 2G segment, followed by Lava at 30% and HMD at 20%. These are second-quarter figures, not a measure of current festive demand.Talapatra nevertheless expects migration towards 4G to accelerate. He said itel was expanding digital-payment support and larger displays, while inexpensive 2G handsets retained a role as backup calling devices.HMD similarly sees better connectivity and payments as ways to extend the category’s usefulness. Older users value familiar controls, while some smartphone owners want a break from notifications and social media. Kunwar identified digital detox as another reason for buying basic phones, although he provided no figures establishing its scale.For manufacturers, the task is to make these devices more useful while preserving the low cost and simplicity that keep customers buying them.
Article Summary: Rising smartphone prices put upgrades beyond some buyers’ budgets. Counterpoint Research’s October 23 report showed shipments below Rs 20,000 falling 47% year- on-year in July–September. Around 200 million people still use 2G feature phones in India.

Article Title: IIT Kharagpur highlights success of Nagar Udyam initiative through campus pilot
Article Text: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur has highlighted the success of its Nagar Udyam initiative that was launched as a pilot within the campus during Durga Puja this year.This is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative, conceptualised by Prof. Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur, through its SETU Cloud Kitchen Connect.The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs, allowing them to do business in a sustainable manner.This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.It enables an entrepreneur to take an entire business home at night and move it towards customers the next morning.Apart from Prof. Chakraborty, Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur and several others, including small entrepreneurs, were present during the inauguration of the project. This is part of the institute's Platinum Jubilee commitment to translate design and technology into tangible social and economic opportunities.The project involves a small three-wheeled cart that can be towed by the owner's motorcycle. This will enable the entrepreneur to move to where there is demand. It has a range of about 30 km, subject to operational and road-safety validation.Once the day's business is done, the home-storage unit can be taken home, thereby clearing up public road space. The cart has solar-cum-battery renewal-energy-enabled essential low-power functions, with compact battery storage.The carts have the SETU digital backbone, including QR-enabled identification, cashless payments, training and pathways to financial inclusion. They also have built-in hygiene, with protected food display, food-grade surfaces and three-way waste segregation.Through the campus demonstration, IIT Kharagpur hopes to replicate the model across West Bengal, allowing street vendors to operate with dignity, without getting into trouble with the authorities.The compact vending structure can be towed by the owner behind a motorcycle, positioned at suitable places of concentrated demand and taken back home after business hours.A vendor could potentially cater to commuters in one part of the day and to a campus or community gathering later, without being tied to a costly permanent storefront. Its proposed mobility over roughly 30 kilometres offers a route to wider customer access.This changes the equation for both livelihoods and urban space. Rather than treating the entrepreneur’s business and pedestrian accessibility as competing priorities, the design aims for flexible, appropriately authorised vending that does not permanently claim a portion of the road.Further envisaged elements include food-safety status access, grievance redressal and data-assisted governance.“Our ambition is not simply to redesign a street cart; it is to redesign the opportunity around the person who runs it. A business that can move with demand, return home at night and connect to clean energy and digital finance can turn an opportunity seeker into a job creator. That is the kind of technology translation IIT Kharagpur stands for," Prof Chakraborty had said during the launch.The initiative suggests a fresh approach to public-space management: vending with clearer identification, better food practices, mobility and reduced permanent obstruction. These benefits will depend on practical traffic safeguards, lawful operating locations and coordination with civic authorities.As stated by Shri Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur, “The best solutions for our streets must protect livelihoods as well as public safety. A mobile, identifiable and responsibly operated vending unit offers an interesting way to reduce permanent obstruction while preserving economic opportunity. The key will be disciplined implementation, safe movement and compliance with local rules.”The launch at the IIT Kharagpur campus evaluated food safety, operational efficiency, environmental performance, mobility, vendor experience and consumer response.Evidence from the pilot is intended to inform a prospective West Bengal Smart Street Vendor Framework, covering cart standards, food-safety practices, space management and measurable social outcomes. In this micro-startup vision, someone who cannot afford a permanent shop may still be able to build a business — and, over time, create jobs for others.
Article Summary: Nagar Udyam is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative. The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs. This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.

Tech leaders continue to dominate the global wealth rankings, holding nine of the top 10 positions on the Forbes billionaires list released on November 1. However, a downturn across technology stocks over the past month erased a combined $273 billion from the fortunes of the world’s eight wealthiest individuals. A wave of disappointing corporate earnings and escalating market concerns over massive artificial intelligence (AI) expenditures pushed the tech-heavy Nasdaq down nearly 5%, triggering widespread declines among the industry's most prominent founders and executives. Notably, 9 out of 10 in list are tech executives, with Warren Buffett the only exception.Despite seeing their personal net worths shrink sharply, none of the top-ranking billionaires shifted position on the leaderboard.The planet's richest individual absorbed the steepest hit, shedding an estimated $68 billion. Musk's net worth stood at $869 billion. The decline came as an 11% drop in SpaceX shares, which outpaced a 13% gain in Tesla stock. Even after the contraction, Musk remains more than twice as rich as his closest competitor.Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has seen his net worth drop by an estimated $8 billion to $361 billion after Amazon shares fell 4%.Alphabet’s cofounders saw steep losses after shares of Google's parent company fell by more than 18%. Page dropped roughly $53 billion to sit at $233 billion, while Brin’s wealth shrank by about $49 billion to $214 billion.The bleeding continued for Dell Technologies and Meta. With Dell shares tumbling 21% and Meta sliding 15%, both Michael Dell and Mark Zuckerberg lost an estimated $40 billion each. Their net worths now sit at $229 billion and $211 billion, respectively.Bucking the tech market rout, only two billionaires in the global top 10 expanded their wealth over the past month, maintaining their ranks at the bottom of the elite bracket:Microsoft's former CEO saw his fortune tick up by $1 billion to an estimated $162 billion, supported by a 2% rise in Microsoft stock.The legendary Berkshire Hathaway investor was the month's biggest gainer among the top 10. A 9% jump in Berkshire shares boosted Buffett’s net worth by an estimated $13 billion to $154 billion.(Rankings and fortunes recorded as of November 1, 2026, at 12 a.m. ET)Notably, every member of the current top 10 is an American man. Six individuals hold net worths exceeding $200 billion, with the entry threshold for the elite group standing at $154 billion. Bill Gates dropped out of the top 10 in October 2024 following newly obtained financial disclosures that reduced his estimated net worth.Musk has retained the title of the world’s richest person since late May 2024, when he bypassed France’s Bernard Arnault. In June, Musk briefly made financial history by becoming the world's first trillionaire.Meanwhile, Jeff Bezos secured second place for the second straight month, a spot he previously occupied in May 2025. In September, Bezos became just the fourth person ever to cross the $300 billion threshold, joining Musk, Larry Page and Larry Ellison.Holding a fortune of approximately $133 billion derived from her stake in Walmart, she advanced to the 14th-richest position globally, up from No. 15 last month.
Article Summary: Tech leaders continue to dominate the global wealth rankings, holding nine of the top 10 positions on the Forbes billionaires list released on November 1. Article Title: Palmer Luckey says that California's Wealth tax that has many billionaires leaving the State has become point of friction between him and his friends; says that they are upset that by not leaving Cali
Article Text:
Palmer Luckey, founder of Oculus and Anduril Industries

Palmer Luckey says he is not leaving California

What is California's Proposition 40

Poll Vote & Share your view Should billionaires fight against higher taxes in their state? Yes, they should advocate against it No, they should support taxes for public welfare It depends on how the revenue is used 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Tech entrepreneur Palmer Luckey has said that the California’s proposed billionaire tax for its ultra-rich residents has caused friction between him and his friends. “This has been a point of friction between me and some of my other billionaire friends,” the 34-year-old cofounder of Oculus VR and Anduril said. “They’ve said things like ‘Palmer, you have to have solidarity for us. You can’t enable these really bad policies. If you stay and if you don’t leave, it’s going to show them that there’s no consequences.’ I empathize with that argument, but it’s not one that I’m going to participate in right now because I still believe that we can fix things.” For those unaware, California proposed a wealth tax bill earlier this year. It seeks to impose a one-time, 5% net-worth tax on California residents with a fortune exceeding $1 billion.Palmer Luckey said that while he opposes the bill, he is not leaving California unlike other tech entrepreneurs who have already left the state. Explaining why he thinks it is worth staying, he said during a press conference last week:“I think that this tax act, if you can call it a tax, is going to cause a lot of problems. It’s causing a lot of people to run who I don’t want to be running. It’s going to cause companies that I work with to leave the state, which is a problem for me.”“As of right now, though, I’m not running. I am staying,” he continued. “I think California is something special. I want to fight for California.”Proposition 40 will be on the ballot in November. It would impose a one-time 5% tax on California’s 200 billionaires. Ninety percent of the revenue would go to the state’s health care program. The remaining 10% would go to education, food assistance and administration. The bill has been opposed by several tech leaders including Google cofounders Sergey Brin and Larry Page, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel.
Article Summary: Oculus VR and Anduril Industries cofounder Palmer Luckey says he is not leaving California. California proposed a wealth tax bill earlier this year. It seeks to impose a one-time, 5% net-worth tax on California residents with a fortune exceeding $1 billion.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos' $1 million grant is helping formerly incarcerated young people in Atlanta build farming businesses across 30 Black-owned farms and create 40 jobs
Article Text:
How Jeff Bezos' $1 million grant is supporting Atlanta's formerly incarcerated youth

How the programme combines farming with employment and training

Gangstas to Growers participants take part in hands-on farming activities in Atlanta. (Gangstas to Growers / Bezos Earth Fund)

How Gangstas to Growers is helping participants build businesses

Part of a $7.9 million investment in Atlanta's green spaces

What the organisation has achieved so far

A $1 million grant from Jeff Bezos' Bezos Earth Fund is supporting Gangstas to Growers, an Atlanta-based organisation that uses agriculture to create employment and entrepreneurship opportunities for at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people. Awarded in July 2023, the funding is intended to expand regenerative agricultural production across 30 farms on Black-owned land and create 40 new jobs. The initiative also aims to strengthen local food systems and generate economic activity in West Atlanta. By combining practical farming experience with business education and mentorship, the programme seeks to help participants develop marketable skills and explore pathways towards economic independence while supporting Black-owned farms and community-led food production.Gangstas to Growers, also known as G2G, is an Atlanta-based social enterprise founded by Abiodun Henderson. The organisation uses agriculture as a way to provide employment, entrepreneurship and personal-development opportunities to at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people.The initiative works with Black-owned farms around Atlanta, giving participants opportunities to learn agricultural skills through practical projects.Its approach combines farming with mentorship, business education and personal development, with the broader aim of addressing barriers to employment and reducing recidivism, which refers to returning to criminal behaviour or the criminal justice system after an earlier offence or period of incarceration.The Bezos Earth Fund awarded the $1 million grant in July 2023 to help the organisation expand its agricultural training and infrastructure. According to the fund, G2G plans to expand regenerative agricultural production across 30 farms on Black-owned land and create 40 new jobs for at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people.Participants learn practical agricultural skills, including seeding, growing, harvesting and composting. They receive opportunities to work on projects at Black-owned farms while gaining experience that can help them explore employment and entrepreneurship.The programme extends beyond agricultural instruction. Its curriculum also includes business education, mentorship, yoga, life coaching and arts classes. These activities are designed to help participants develop confidence, leadership abilities and skills that can be applied to different career paths.A December 2024 report by Georgia Public Broadcasting (GPB) documented how participants engage with the programme. It highlighted the experiences of young people who were developing agricultural skills while considering different professional ambitions.Not everyone intends to pursue farming as a full-time career. One participant featured in the report planned to pursue videography while continuing to grow plants at home. Another wanted to develop a business focused on helping people experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity.Beyond providing agricultural training, G2G aims to help participants develop businesses through worker-owned cooperatives. The model gives graduates opportunities to participate in collective ownership and build enterprises connected to local food production.One example is Sweet Sol, a hot sauce business associated with the organisation's graduates. Participants grow and harvest ingredients used to make the product, while the cooperative model connects agricultural production with food processing, product development and sales.According to G2G, proceeds support young people, the programme and Black-owned farms around Atlanta. The initiative demonstrates how agricultural training can lead to opportunities beyond farm work, including developing products and participating in small businesses.The organisation also works towards strengthening community ownership of food-related enterprises, allowing participants to explore business opportunities while contributing to the local economy.The $1 million grant was part of the Bezos Earth Fund's announcement of $7.9 million in funding for urban greening projects in Atlanta on July 17, 2023. The funding supported nine projects intended to improve access to green spaces and strengthen environmental conditions in underserved communities.The wider investment included initiatives involving urban farms, community gardens, native plants, wildlife habitats and agricultural workforce development. It formed part of the fund's $400 million Greening America's Cities initiative, which aims to improve equitable access to urban green spaces through 2030.Another recipient, On Da Farm, received $1 million to support urban farming, native plant cultivation, wildlife habitats and agricultural workforce development. Its plans included training 40 new farmers and 12 farmer apprentices, alongside producing food for local families through its weekly farmers' market.Gangstas to Growers' work fits into this broader strategy by connecting environmental sustainability with employment opportunities, food access and community economic development.Gangstas to Growers reports that its work has resulted in 5,000 pounds of food being harvested, 25 Black-owned farms being serviced and 20 programme graduates.These figures appear in the organisation's published impact summary and reflect its reported activities. Its website does not clearly specify the reporting period for each figure.The initiative has also received independent coverage. In December 2024, GPB reported on a graduating cohort, documenting how participants were developing agricultural skills and considering different career paths through the programme.The Bezos Earth Fund's grant announcement identifies expanding production across 30 Black-owned farms and creating 40 jobs as objectives of the investment. The available reporting does not establish whether these specific targets have been fully achieved.Through agricultural training, paid work and business development, Gangstas to Growers is seeking to create economic opportunities for young people who face barriers to employment while supporting Black-owned farms and strengthening Atlanta's local food system.
Article Summary: Gangstas to Growers is an Atlanta-based social enterprise founded by Abiodun Henderson. It uses agriculture to provide employment, entrepreneurship and personal-development opportunities to at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people. The initiative works with Black-owned farms around Atlanta, giving participants opportunities to learn agricultural skills. Its approach combines farming with mentorship, business education and personal development.

Article Title: Google Pay gets new shopping feature with virtual try-on: What is Discover Shop and how it works
Article Text:
What is Discover Shop

How can users access it on Google Pay

How do virtual try-on and image search work

Google Pay is testing a shopping feature in India. Named Discover Shop, the experience introduces a personalised fashion and lifestyle feed inside the payments app, combining product listings, YouTube videos, visual search and AI-powered virtual try-on. Google says the pilot is currently available to a limited number of users as it gathers feedback.Eligible users can browse recommendations based on their consented Google activity, upload an image to find similar products and preview how select clothing items might look on them. Product discovery takes place within Google Pay, while purchases are completed on merchants’ websites using the shopper’s preferred payment method. Access also requires a personal Google Account with Web & App Activity and Search Personalization enabled.Discover Shop gives users a dedicated space to explore fashion products and styling content tailored to their preferences. Google says the experience draws on its Shopping Graph, a continually updated collection of information covering more than 60 billion products.The feed combines shopping recommendations with YouTube videos.Users can open individual listings to view details such as colour, size and other available options.Google is also bringing visual search and virtual try-on into the experience, allowing users to explore products through images as well as browse their personalised feed.Users can check availability by updating Google Pay to the latest version and looking for the Discover or Discover Shop icon at the bottom of the screen.Those with access can open the tab to load their feed and select a product for more information. The feature requires users to be signed into a personal Google Account and have both Web & App Activity and Search Personalization switched on.Updating the app does not guarantee access, as the rollout remains limited to selected users in India.For supported products, users can open a listing and select Try it on, followed by Try on you, to see an AI-generated preview of how the item looks on them. Google says it also plans to introduce pre-generated daily looks for outfit suggestions. That addition is described as coming soon.To find similar styles, users can select Search and point the camera at an item. They can also upload a photograph to discover visually similar products across the web.When a shopper selects an item they want to buy, the experience directs them to the merchant’s website to complete the transaction. Google says shoppers can use their preferred payment method there.
Article Summary: Discover Shop gives users a dedicated space to explore fashion products and styling content tailored to their preferences. Google says the experience draws on its Shopping Graph, a continually updated collection of information covering more than 60 billion products. Users can open individual listings to view details such as colour, size and other available options.

Article Title: After offering buyouts to 60,000 employees, Microsoft is borrowing $25 billion to pay for AI; CFO Amy Hood says: We’re fortunate to have...
Article Text:
Microsoft raises $25 billion in bonds days after offering exit packages to 60,000 staff

Microsoft’s $25 billion bond sale drew $115 billion in orders

The voluntary exit offer covers staff in India, the US, Canada and the UK

Amy Hood expects 3,000 or fewer employees to take the buyout

Microsoft has priced a $25 billion bond sale, its first US investment-grade offering since 2017, just three days after it offered voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 employees. The company says the money will go towards general corporate purposes, including capital expenditure, as its AI data centre bills keep climbing.The sequence is hard to miss. On the earnings call on Wednesday, CFO Amy Hood said, “We’re fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our ratings are, and we haven’t yet tapped that.” The notes were priced a day later in ten tranches maturing between 2028 and 2066, and they are set to close on November 4.Orders peaked at $115 billion, about 4.6 times the amount on offer, according to people familiar with the deal. Fixed-rate coupons run from 4.85 percent on $2 billion of notes due 2028 to 6.35 percent on $2 billion of notes due 2066. Two tranches are floating-rate notes worth $1 billion each.Investors had a clear reason to line up. Microsoft and Johnson & Johnson are the only publicly traded US companies with AAA ratings from both Moody’s and S&P.Microsoft last borrowed in this market in 2017, when it raised $17 billion.It is also the first sale from a major hyperscaler since Alphabet priced $25 billion of debt in August. Meta chose equity instead, raising $25 billion that way. Microsoft also stands apart on cash: it reported positive free cash flow for the quarter, while Alphabet, Meta and Amazon reported negative figures. Hyperscalers and data centre developers had already raised more than $313 billion through investment-grade bonds globally this year, nearly three times the full-year 2025 total.Microsoft announced the offer on October 26 for eligible employees at level 70 and below in participating teams. That is more than a quarter of its 223,000 full-time workforce. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said it lets employees “make that transition now with support.” Microsoft calls it time-limited and voluntary.A source familiar with the plan said eligible teams include AI experiences, Copilot, finance, HR, Xbox and Windows + Devices. Marketing, commercial business and security are excluded.A Microsoft spokesperson said the company expects 3,000 or fewer takers, which is 5 percent or less of those eligible. Hood addressed staff questions in her quarterly earnings memo. She wrote that the aim is to offer employees “agency if they choose to leave the company on their own terms,” and that “we expect very few people to select this offer because of the growth opportunities here at Microsoft.”Earlier this year, a voluntary retirement offer to about 9,000 US employees was accepted by roughly one-third of those eligible, which helped Microsoft cut fewer people in later layoffs. In July, the company announced 4,800 job cuts, or about 2.1 percent of its workforce, while overhauling Xbox.The quarter itself gave Hood plenty to work with. Revenue grew 19 percent, operating income rose 21 percent and Azure revenue climbed 48 percent. She said Azure demand continues to exceed supply, and thanked engineering teams working to deliver capacity faster. Microsoft has forecast about $175 billion in capital expenditure for 2026. That is the bill both moves are meant to help cover. Microsoft will detail its AI and cloud plans at Ignite from November 17 to 20.
Article Summary: Microsoft’s $25 billion bond sale drew $115 billion in orders. The voluntary exit offer covers staff in India, the US, Canada and the UK. CFO Amy Hood expects 3,000 or fewer employees to take the buyout. Microsoft and Johnson & Johnson are the only publicly traded US companies with AAA ratings.

Article Title: Hackers hit Nvidia’s cloud development platform: What the company said in notification sent to affected customers
Article Text:
Nvidia

What Nvidia told affected users: Read notification

We are writing to inform you that NVIDIA Corporation ("NVIDIA") has experienced a security incident that may affect the security of your data. NVIDIA is providing this notice to you with details of the incident, our response, and resources available to you to help protect your personal information from possible misuse.

What Happened?

Our incident investigation identified unauthorized activity affecting the NVIDIA Brev platform from October 4 through October 20, 2026. We acted to secure our systems and to determine the information potentially affected. Our analysis determined that your information from our Brev network may have been affected.

What Information Was Involved?

Our analysis determined that the following information was potentially exposed: the SSH key that Brev provisioned for your Brev-provisioned VM.

This SSH key has since been rotated, and your instances have been updated with the replacement key. At this time, we are unaware of improper use of these keys.

Nvidia has been hit by another cyberattack, this time targeting its Brev cloud development platform. According to a report, unauthorised activity occurred on the service between October 4 and October 20, prompting the company to send formal breach notifications to affected users warning that their account information may have been exposed. Citing the customer notice, Tom’s Hardware reported that Nvidia launched an internal investigation after spotting unidentified activity on the platform. The probe determined that malicious actors may have accessed data stored on Brev systems, specifically compromising Secure Shell (SSH) keys configured by the service.In its communication to users, Nvidia confirmed the security breach and outlined the immediate technical steps taken to protect developer systems, while also stating that it replaced the compromised SSH keys with new credentials. The company added that its team has found no evidence showing the exposed keys were improperly used.The breach at Nvidia arrives amid a broader series of security incidents aimed at AI infrastructure providers and developer cloud platforms. For example, on October 30, cybersecurity firm Wiz published a report detailing what it described as a “Black October” for AI developer services. The firm tracked security incidents across at least nine platforms throughout the month.
Article Summary: N Nvidia has been hit by another cyberattack, this time targeting its Brev cloud development platform. According to a report, unauthorised activity occurred on the service between October 4 and October 20, prompting the company to send formal breach notifications to affected users. The probe determined that malicious actors may have accessed data stored on Brev systems.

Diwali is when most people go out and buy something new for their homes, and more often than not it is a new TV. For others it is a soundbar to complete a home theatre they have been building, a full sound system, or at times the entire setup in one go. This list has all of it: five TVs, five sound systems and a streaming device, 11 products in total, for you to pick from depending on whether your room needs a better picture, fuller sound or a smarter way to stream.Start with what bothers you most. If it is the screen, the TVs here come in sizes and styles to suit different rooms. If it is the sound, the options run from a soundbar system and a pair of powered speakers to full surround setups, one of which also plays music in other rooms. If the TV is fine but the experience feels slow, the streaming device is a small fix.You do not have to buy it all. Pick one piece, or put the whole setup together over time. Here is what each product offers, so you can decide what your living room needs.Rs 1,34,990Samsung’s Micro RGB technology uses individually controlled red, green and blue micro LEDs to manage light and colour. The company says this is designed to deliver vivid colours and detailed images across different types of content, and it presents the technology as a change in how colour is reproduced and how the picture is processed.The 55-inch R85H is a 4K smart TV from the 2026 range with AI-powered picture optimisation and intelligent sound features, in a slim body meant for contemporary living rooms. Glare Free technology, which reduces reflections, is available only on select models, and Vision AI features for picture optimisation and content experiences vary by model, so the exact feature set of a given unit is worth confirming before purchase.Rs 1,60,261The C6 uses LG’s alpha 11 AI Processor Gen3 with a Dual AI Engine, which controls the panel’s 8.3 million self-lit pixels. LG says the NPU is up to 5.6 times faster than before, with the CPU 50% faster and the GPU 70% stronger. A Brightness Booster feature lifts highlights, and the panel carries UL-verified Perfect Black and Perfect Color, with certification for 100% colour volume and fidelity. On the gaming side it supports up to 165Hz at 4K with G-Sync compatibility and FreeSync Premium, a 0.1ms response time, VESA-certified DSC, Nvidia GeForce Now and a Game Dashboard. webOS adds an AI Hub with Multi AI Search using Gemini and Copilot, plus AI Concierge and voice profiles. The set is 45.1mm deep without its stand, and the webOS Re:New programme promises up to five years of software upgrades.Rs 3,59,900The 7 II uses what Sony calls True RGB, where red, green and blue LEDs in the backlight are controlled independently. Sony says this combines the colour range of its QD-OLED TVs with the brightness of Mini LED, and X-Wide Angle Pro keeps colour and contrast steady from side seats. The XR Processor with AI handles 4K upscaling and fast motion, and the TV supports IMAX Enhanced, Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos. A subwoofer, rear speakers or both can connect directly to the TV through BRAVIA Theatre, without a soundbar. For gaming, it offers 4K at 120fps and PS5 features such as Auto HDR Tone Mapping, though VRR support varies by model. It runs Google TV and comes in sizes from 55 to 98 inches.The Vision 9 is the biggest Lumio TV yet, a 65-inch QD-MiniLED set from the 2026 range. Lumio has put much of its pitch into speed. It runs a MediaTek Pentonic 700 chip with 3GB of RAM, and the company says the TV boots in seconds. Storage is 64GB, which Lumio says is 50 per cent faster than before, so apps install and load quicker. A Wi-Fi chip is meant to keep streaming smooth. On the software side, the TV runs TLDR 2.0, Lumio’s own content discovery platform, which pulls together trending titles and recommendations across apps. The remote has a dedicated TLDR button to open it. Lumio is also offering a free third year of warranty on the 65-inch model, and its Diwali sale offers are live on the site.Rs 79,990Hisense’s U7SE is a 4K Mini LED TV, and the 55-inch is the smallest of four sizes that go up to 85 inches. It uses a Hi-QLED panel and a Total HDR solution for picture quality. Gamers get a native 144Hz mode, and a built-in subwoofer adds some bass without an extra box. It runs on VIDAA, Hisense’s own smart TV platform, and supports hands-free voice control. If you want a Mini LED screen and a larger size, the same series covers it.Rs 22,999The Aura 5 is a pair of powered speakers, not a soundbar. It uses 4.5-inch woofers and 1-inch silk dome tweeters in wooden enclosures, and the amplifier and DAC sit inside the right speaker, so no receiver is needed. That speaker also carries every input: HDMI ARC with CEC, optical, coaxial, USB, RCA/AUX and Bluetooth 5.4. Connect it to the TV over HDMI and the TV remote controls the volume. Lumio quotes a 35Hz to 20kHz response and lossless playback up to 24-bit/48kHz. The supplied cable between the two speakers is 2 metres, which sets how far apart they can sit unless you use your own wire.Rs 60,000Sonodyne has been making audio gear in India since 1970, and the SAMA 6000 is its 5.1-channel Dolby Atmos system. The soundbar carries five full-range drivers for the left, right, centre and side-firing surround channels. The wireless subwoofer has an 8-inch driver, and total output is 700W. One HDMI eARC cable connects it to the TV, and the subwoofer pairs automatically. HDMI in, optical, AUX and Bluetooth are also on offer. Three EQ modes cover movies, music and dialogue, the subwoofer level can be adjusted separately, and the system carries a two-year warranty.Rs 1,10,990The Q990H is an 11.1.4-channel system, meaning 11 front and surround channels, one subwoofer channel and four up-firing channels. The bar itself has front-firing, side-firing and up-firing speakers, and the box includes a subwoofer with dual 20.32 cm units and AI Dynamic Bass Control, plus two wireless rear speakers that can face front or back. Dolby Atmos is transmitted wirelessly over Wi-Fi with 2022 to 2026 Samsung TVs, and Eclipsa Audio is supported. Q-Symphony plays sound through the TV and soundbar together, SpaceFit Sound Pro tunes the output to the room, and Active Voice Amplifier Pro raises dialogue over background noise. Other features include Game Pro mode, Private Rear Sound for late-night viewing, HDMI 2.1 with eARC, Google Cast, AirPlay, Spotify Connect and SmartThings.Rs 1,83,997This set bundles four products: the Arc Ultra soundbar, the Sub 4 wireless subwoofer and two Era 100 smart speakers. Sonos describes it as plug and play, with setup done through the Sonos app once the products are powered on. The speakers can be mixed and matched, so the system can serve both the TV and music in other parts of the home, and more Sonos products can be added later. The Arc Ultra is priced at Rs 84,999 on its own, the Sub 4 at Rs 67,999 and each Era 100 at Rs 21,999. The retailer lists delivery within six to seven business days.Rs 2,39,990The Trio is Sony’s flagship wireless home theatre system, and it takes a different approach from a soundbar. Dedicated left, centre and right speakers are meant to create a wider soundstage than a single bar, and Sony says the layout is aimed at today’s very large TVs. It supports Dolby Atmos and DTS and integrates with compatible BRAVIA televisions. The figure of up to 24 phantom speakers applies when it is paired with the Sub 9 and Rear 9. The Sub 9 is a 600W subwoofer with dual opposing drivers, priced at Rs 94,990, and the Rear 9 has large up-firing speakers and a swivel wall-mount bracket, priced at Rs 74,990. Both are sold separately.Rs 39,900 (2026 model, pre-order); Rs 16,900 (2022 model)The Apple TV 4K is not a necessary addition to a home theatre, but it is a worthwhile one. It is a small streaming box that plugs into the HDMI port of any TV above and brings Apple TV, Apple Music, Apple Arcade and Photos to the screen, with 4K Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and Dolby Atmos in supported apps. The 2026 model swaps the 2022 model’s A15 chip for an A19, adds Wi-Fi 7 and a far-field microphone for Siri AI, and works as a smart home hub with HomeKit and Matter accessories. It is on pre-order from 13 November at Rs 39,900, more than twice the Rs 16,900 at which the 2022 model is listed at one retailer, and Apple says Siri AI also works on the second-generation box and later. If you want one this Diwali, the 2022 model is the one to look for, provided it costs less than the new one.
Article Summary: Diwali is when most people go out and buy something new for their homes. For others it is a soundbar to complete a home theatre they have been building, or a full sound system. This list has five TVs, five sound systems and a streaming device, 11 products in total.

Article Title: From turning first dates into interviews to using ChatGPT for replies and tracking matches in spreadsheets: How AI companies are changing San Francisco’s dating scene
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

When first dates become interviews

“You don’t need to understand if they have cancer in their family; you don’t need to understand on the first date if they really want three children,”

ChatGPT replies and spreadsheets for matches

Singles are trying alternatives to dating apps

San Francisco’s artificial intelligence (AI) boom is changing how some residents date. AI company founders and engineers working long hours are bringing their professional habits into their personal lives, screening potential partners against detailed criteria and approaching first meetings like interviews. According to a New York Times report, some also use ChatGPT to review messages and analyse their dating history, while others link dating-app data to spreadsheets to track matches.The report describes a dating scene shaped by limited free time and pressure to find a suitable partner quickly. A coach charging tech founders $5,000 a month frames dating in business metrics, while some workers struggle to fit meetings into demanding schedules. For those seeking relationships, the habits used to build a company can make getting to know someone feel like another work task.Mehul Agarwal, the 24-year-old co-founder of AI filmmaking startup Koyal, described one date that took two months to schedule. Both worked at AI startups and arrived exhausted. Their familiarity with professional small talk made the evening feel like a networking meeting.Agarwal wants to find a wife before becoming wealthy, so he will not have to question whether a partner is attracted to his success.But work and travel have limited his opportunities to build a relationship.Other daters described being assessed against a checklist. Amanda Chung, 25, who works at AI startup Nectar Social, said one founder could meet only after 10 p.m. Another asked about her job and work style.Sina Hartung, a co-founder of Eureka Health, asked how much some people expect to establish right away.she told NYT.Joyce Zhang, a former Stripe product manager who now coaches tech founders on dating, said some clients treat finding a partner as a problem money and optimisation can solve.She uses familiar business language, discussing their “top of funnel”, meaning the pool of potential partners, and the proportion of connections that become dates.Some clients link dating-app information to spreadsheets. Others focus on understanding the apps’ algorithms or run replies through ChatGPT. Some give the chatbot their entire dating history and ask it to identify patterns. Zhang said her coaching encourages clients to trust their intuition rather than rely entirely on analysis.Some residents are organising events that give people another way to meet. At Kilowatt, a bar in San Francisco’s Mission neighbourhood, participants at a “Date My Ex” event used short slide presentations to introduce potential partners to the audience.The event is part of a “Date My Friend” series organised by Annalise Wulf and two friends as an alternative to apps and a response to demanding dating criteria.Wulf said long startup hours leave little room for connections that develop gradually. Many AI startup workers follow a “996” schedule: 9 am to 9 pm, six days a week.
Article Summary: AI company founders and engineers working long hours are bringing their professional habits into their personal lives. They are screening potential partners against detailed criteria and approaching first meetings like interviews. Some also use ChatGPT to review messages and analyse their dating history. Others link dating-app data to spreadsheets to track matches.

Article Title: Dell CEO Michael Dell, biggest contributor to Trump Accounts, advice to businesses on what never to ask other people
Article Text:
Michael Dell: If you go and ask people, most will tell you no

From a dorm room to a $302 billion company

Embracing risk and failure

Early entrepreneurial instincts

Building a $302 billion company

Michael Dell, the founder and CEO of Dell Technologies and one of the biggest contributors to the Trump Accounts initiative, has a simple piece of advice for entrepreneurs and business leaders: don't ask other people whether your big idea is a good one. Speaking in an interview with Fortune, Dell said that breakthrough businesses are often built on ideas that others initially dismiss. According to the billionaire executive, entrepreneurs should focus on creating something unique and differentiated instead of seeking validation from people who may not share their vision. His point is that most people will dismiss anything unfamiliar, so he says to trust your own instincts about whether a product or business will succeed over the long run. Fortune has revisited his advice now that his company is valued at $302 billion as of October 30. Dell also told Fortune that to make it big, an idea has to be unique, and differentiated from anything others are doing.Reflecting on his entrepreneurial journey, Dell said risk-taking played a crucial role in building what has become a technology company valued at more than $300 billion."If you want to really make it big, you better come up with something unique," Dell told Fortune.He added that successful ideas need to be differentiated from what everyone else is doing.His strongest advice, however, was directed at founders looking for approval before launching a product or business. "If you go and ask people if it's a good idea, most of them will tell you no," Dell said. "So don't go ask." According to Dell, entrepreneurs should trust their instincts and vision rather than relying too heavily on external opinions, especially in the early stages of building a business.Dell took up pre-med at the University of Texas in 1983 to please his parents, according to Entrepreneur, but he had long been fascinated by computers. According to the 1999 biography Direct From Dell, he took apart an Apple II at 15 to see how it worked. At 19, he began selling PC upgrade kits to other students in his dorm, which launched his business. Like Apple’s Steve Jobs, he was a college dropout.He started with just $1,000, and his manufacturing team consisted of “three guys with screwdrivers sitting at six-foot tables,” he said in the book. “You have to embrace risk, and you have to accept failure,” he told Fortune.Dell says a willingness to take risks has remained central to his leadership philosophy. "You have to embrace risk, and you have to accept failure," he told Fortune, arguing that excessive focus on avoiding risk often stifles innovation. The billionaire contrasted entrepreneurial thinking with the approach commonly found inside large corporations, where risk management frequently takes precedence over experimentation."Big companies generally aren't good at taking risks," Dell said. "If you talk about risk, they'll talk about the risk reduction, and the risk committee, and the risk management, and all those say the risk is bad. Well, if you don't have risk, you don't have innovation."Long before founding Dell Technologies, Dell displayed an entrepreneurial streak while attending high school in Houston. He sold newspaper subscriptions for the Houston Post and developed a targeted marketing strategy focused on newly married couples.By identifying households most likely to subscribe and reaching them through direct-mail campaigns, Dell reportedly earned $18,000 in a single year, more than some of his teachers were making at the time. The experience would later influence Dell's direct-sales business model, helping the company become the world's largest PC maker by 2001.Dell's company has undergone multiple transformations over the decades. After taking the company private in a $24.4 billion buyout in 2013, Dell orchestrated the $67 billion acquisition of EMC, one of the largest technology deals ever completed. Today, Dell Technologies has a market value of roughly $302 billion, while Michael Dell's personal fortune is estimated at around $234 billion.Last year, Dell and his wife, Susan Dell, pledged $6.25 billion to help seed Trump Accounts for millions of American children, making them among the largest contributors to the initiative. Despite building one of the world's most valuable technology companies, Dell says the formula for innovation has remained unchanged: take risks, accept failure and avoid seeking permission for every bold idea. "We've got hundreds of projects, and they're not all going to work out," Dell told Fortune. "That's okay."
Article Summary: Michael Dell is the founder and CEO of Dell Technologies, a technology company valued at $302 billion. In an interview with Fortune, Dell said breakthrough businesses are often built on ideas that others initially dismiss. According to Dell, entrepreneurs should trust their instincts and vision rather than relying too heavily on external opinions.

Article Title: Weeks after hackers hit hundreds of French supermarkets, freezers at Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg grocery stores overheat
Article Text:
Freezers at Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg grocery stores overheat

Several retail chains report overnight disruptions

‘Echoes’ of France's hacking attack in October

Supermarket refrigerators and freezers across Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg saw temperatures climb sharply overnight, triggering widespread alarm over a potential second cyberattack on European grocery retail, a report has said. The incident comes just weeks after an October incident in France knocked out cold-storage systems at hundreds of supermarkets, spoiling millions of euros worth of food inventory. As per a report by The Guardian, technicians scrambled in the wee hours to keep units from overheating further.Several grocery brands confirmed unexpected temperature spikes inside store chillers and freezers. At least one said cyberattacks affected supermarket fridges in Belgium and Sweden.In Belgium and Luxembourg, Dutch retail group Ahold Delhaize, which reported a separate cybersecurity incident to Dutch police last month, disclosed that an “IT incident” impacted cooling units across dozens of its locations. Ahold Delhaize spokesperson Sarah De Meester confirmed cooling temperatures had increased and stated that an active investigation is underway.Similarly, Belgian daily Le Soir reported disruptions across dozens of outlets, including five Spar supermarkets, several Shop & Go convenience stores situated at Q8 petrol stations and multiple Proxy Delhaize neighbourhood shops.In Sweden, grocery giant Coop informed Swedish outlet Aftonbladet that six of its locations suffered temperature issues overnight. Competing grocer ICA noted it was aware of a “limited number of stores” affected by an overnight incident that disrupted their refrigeration and freezer controls.Technicians scrambled in the early morning hours to keep units from overheating further.“We started mobilising technicians at 1am. We spent all night and morning disconnecting the affected installations from the grid,” said Stephan Moelans, chief executive of cooling systems specialist Sabcobel, in an interview with Le Soir.The latest wave of freezer failures essentially mirrors a cyberattack that struck French grocers in October. French law enforcement confirmed that hackers breached cooling equipment at up to 700 supermarkets, overriding thousands of commercial freezers, fridges and display cabinets.During the French breach, remote attackers manipulated temperature configurations, elevating chilled storage units from normal levels as low as -27°C to well over 50°C. Threat actors disabled internal alarm mechanisms prior to altering thermostat readings or stretching defrost cycles by hours.The Paris prosecutor’s office launched a formal investigation into the French attacks. Meanwhile, the Pentagon officials said the military investigators have been in touch with their French counterparts about the cyberattack on commercial freezers.
Article Summary: Several grocery brands confirmed unexpected temperature spikes inside store chillers and freezers. At least one said cyberattacks affected supermarket fridges in Belgium and Sweden. The latest wave of freezer failures essentially mirrors a cyberattack that struck French grocers in October.

Article Title: Palantir’s Alex Karp is now a forest owner: Buys 37,000 acres in Sweden for reported $22 million; why hunters can no longer enter it
Article Text:
Palantir CEO Alex Karp

Why hunters can no longer enter the forest that Alex Karp bought

Palantir CEO Alex Karp has purchased 15,000 hectares (37,000 acres) of forest in Härjedalen, Sweden, through his newly registered company Cladonia Skog AB. As reported by Swedish newspaper Tidningen Härjedalen, the sale was reportedly for 235 million kronor, or $22 million. As per the report, hunters in the region had received notifications in the mail alerting them they could no longer lease the land to hunt south of the quiet village of Storsjö Kapell, known for its hiking and fishing. The sale was later confirmed by Svenska Cellulosa Aktiebolaget (SCA), a paper manufacturer that previously owned the land.In an emailed statement to Fortune then, SCA spokesperson Robert Östholm said: “We grant hunting rights through lease agreements with a term of approximately 11 months. This means that the agreements can be reviewed and renewed on an annual basis”.“As we have now sold the land in question, we can of course no longer grant hunting rights on it, as the land is no longer owned by us”.Jenny Lopes Da Silva, a board member of Cladonia and a sales manager at Scandinavian Trust, said in a statement said “The new owner of the forest property is committed to the beauty of the land and its preservation.The vast, natural forest landscapes offer valuable habitats for plants and animals, while also serving as a place for recreation and restoration.”Alex Karp had long ties with Sweden through his company Palantir, which has a partnership with Swedish defense authorities. The company expanded its software-development offering in Europe about a decade ago. However, the EU’s continued use of the company’s services has raised concerns given Europe’s plans to break itself off the US technology and AI.
Article Summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp has purchased 15,000 hectares (37,000 acres) of forest in Härjedalen, Sweden. The sale was reportedly for 235 million kronor, or $22 million. hunters in the region had received notifications in the mail alerting them they could no longer lease the land.

Article Title: CEO of $300 billion cybersecurity company ‘warns’ of more hacking, shares 3 key points on what has changed and advice to companies
Article Text:
Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks

What has changed: 3 key points behind the surge

Attacks will accelerate from here on - We are there: Six months ago I said

Mythos

like capability will be widely available. It's happening. A critical vulnerability, a social engineering attack that looks innocuous, or daisy chaining publicly available vulnerabilities and conducting a sniper strike is all being witnessed in the wild. Incident responders have never been busier.

Some key points:

- attacks are not becoming more sophisticated, it's the same attacks, faster and by a lot more people.

- attack path discovery which took trial and error and multiple attempts is now trivial, open source LLMs are here to help

- you are as secure as your supply chain, insecure down or upstream players who have access to your infrastructure could be the next attack path, marketplaces and supply chain is an easier vector

Nikesh Arora’s advice to companies

The increase in activity is a result of more people becoming better at hacking due to the ease of being able to attack.

Had not contemplated that in my calculus.

Please:

1. Test your infrastructure for accessible vulnerabilities and misconfigurations

2. Fix your code and demand your vendors do.

3. Old infra, or insecure infra at the perimeter needs to be updated first

4. New AI tools, especially coding need a security framework. Your developers will do more with code, new skills, and more automation. Don't forget the coding models have trained on human code.

Nikesh Arora, the CEO of $300 billion cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks, has sounded an alarm on a sharp increase in cyberattacks, warning that hacking incidents will accelerate rapidly from here on out. The top executive recounted that he sounded the alarm six months ago, highlighting that incident response teams will be busier than ever as high-level, AI-powered capabilities become widely available. His comments came days after responders scrambled to patch critical vulnerabilities found in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications.Contrary to common assumptions, the underlying methods behind these intrusions have not turned entirely exotic. Instead, the sudden spike is driven by volume, speed and automation.To defend against the incoming wave of activity, the executive laid out clear operational guidance for leadership teams and security professionals:
Article Summary: CEO of $300 billion cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks, has sounded an alarm on a sharp increase in cyberattacks. Nikesh Arora warns that hacking incidents will accelerate rapidly from here on out. The top executive recounted that he sounded the alarm six months ago, highlighting that incident response teams will be busier than ever.
