Article Title: Apple CEO John Ternus takes a different approach to AI race, says for Apple what matters is…
Article Text:
Apple CEO John Ternus

Apple CEO rejects AI ‘agent’ takeover

Focus on security and privacy over regulation debates

As tech giants race to deploy artificial intelligence (AI) tools and autonomous agents across every layer of computing, Apple ’s new CEO John Ternus is taking a sharply different path. He took the helm of the company during a time of significant technological disruption in its 50-year history. Ternus made it clear that Apple will not chase AI simply for the sake of following industry trends. Instead, he argued that the real test is user experience, not the technology powering it behind the scenes.“Everyone has an opinion – I really like where we’re at,” Ternus said in an interview with Wired. He added: “I would hope people recognise that the work we do is building incredible products that make their lives better. We’re absolutely going to leverage AI to do that. We don't want to ship AI for AI's sake. When we're doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?”While rivals like Google , Microsoft, Meta and OpenAI pour resources into tools designed to write code, replace entire workflows, generate autonomous content and deploy independent agents that act without asking, another faction predicts AI will completely absorb the traditional app ecosystem.Ternus dismissed this narrative, pushed back on the idea of removing humans from the process.“That could make life really easy, I suppose, but the creation of products is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do,” Ternus stated.The stance creates a visible contrast between Apple and the rest of Silicon Valley. While competitors push to automate workflows and substitute human labour with AI models, Ternus is drawing a line between pure automation and human craftsmanship, asserting that product creation still hinges on taste, judgment and human involvement.Addressing questions regarding AI regulation, Ternus steered the focus back toward device integrity, cybersecurity and protecting consumer privacy.“We all read the stories and think about it from a cybersecurity standpoint—clearly these models are very capable of doing things. Our focus is on making sure that our products are secure and safe, and protecting the users' information,” Ternus said.
Article Summary: Apple CEO John Ternus says the real test is user experience, not the technology powering it behind the scenes. The stance creates a visible contrast between Apple and the rest of Silicon Valley. While competitors push to automate workflows and substitute human labour with AI models, Ternu is drawing a line between pure automation and human craftsmanship.

Article Title: GSMA reappoints Airtel Vice Chairman Gopal Vittal as board chair until 2028
Article Text:
Gopal Vittal

The GSMA Board of Directors has re-elected Gopal Vittal, Executive Vice Chairman of Bharti Airtel , as Chair for the 2027-2028 board term, extending his leadership of the global mobile industry body until December 2028. The announcement also confirmed the appointment of Margherita Della Valle, Chief Executive Officer of Vodafone Group, as co-Deputy Chair alongside Ralph Mupita, President and CEO of MTN Group, who was re-elected to the role.Vittal has served on the GSMA Board for a decade and has been Chair since 2025. In the role, he oversees the strategic direction of the organisation, which represents mobile network operators and companies across the broader mobile ecosystem. Commenting on his re-election, Vittal said the telecommunications industry is entering a new phase shaped by advanced networks, artificial intelligence and open digital platforms. However, he stressed that security would remain the industry's highest priority.According to Vittal, the sector must focus on securing nations against growing cyber threats, protecting customers from the rising threat of scams and ensuring the long-term sustainability of the telecom industry so it can continue investing in next-generation infrastructure and technologies.He added that he looks forward to working closely with fellow board members and co-Deputy Chairs Ralph Mupita and Margherita Della Valle during the new term.As Executive Vice Chairman of Bharti Airtel, Vittal oversees the company's operations and subsidiaries while driving strategy across technology, digital services, procurement, networks and talent management. He also serves as Non-Executive Chair of Airtel Africa and Airtel Payments Bank, and is a Non-Executive Director on the BT Group Board. Under his leadership, Airtel has expanded its presence across mobile services, home broadband, enterprise solutions and digital services, strengthening its position in one of the world's most competitive telecom markets.The GSMA's leadership team for the new term will include Ralph Mupita and Margherita Della Valle as co-Deputy Chairs. Mupita has led MTN Group since September 2020 and has served as a GSMA Deputy Chair since April 2025. He is also a Commissioner on the Broadband Commission for Sustainable Development and a founding Commissioner of the International Telecommunication Union's AI for Good Global Commission. He is currently spearheading MTN's Ambition 2030 strategy focused on connectivity, fintech and digital infrastructure growth across Africa.Meanwhile, Margherita Della Valle has been CEO of Vodafone Group since January 2023, after previously serving as the company's Chief Financial Officer. She has led Vodafone's transformation efforts aimed at simplifying operations and strengthening the business.The re-election comes at a time when the global mobile industry is increasingly focused on deploying advanced network technologies, integrating AI into telecom operations and expanding digital services. Under Vittal's continued leadership, the GSMA is expected to place particular emphasis on security, customer protection and industry sustainability, while supporting the development of emerging technologies and digital ecosystems worldwide.
Article Summary: Vittal has served on the GSMA Board for a decade and has been Chair since 2025. He oversees the strategic direction of the organisation, which represents mobile network operators and companies across the broader mobile ecosystem. The announcement also confirmed the appointment of Margherita Della Valle, Chief Executive Officer of Vodafone Group, as co-Deputy Chair.

Article Title: CEO of America's largest bank Jamie Dimon told companies from the stage of investors conference in Europe: Get rid of managers who …
Article Text:
JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon

Jamie Dimon on signs of bureaucracy in an organisation

CEO of America’s largest bank Jamie Dimon asked companies to get rid of managers who favor process over execution. Speaking earlier this year during an investor conference in Europe, Jamie Dimon warned that bureaucracy can quietly undermine organizations from within. "Bureaucracy, complacency and arrogance will take down a company," he said at Norges Bank Investment Management's investment conference in Oslo on April 28. Dimon further warned that organizations irrespective of their size can be affected by bureaucracy, if leaders fail to address it early. So what is the solution? Jamie Dimon said that the solution should start with management accountability and removing leaders who become too attached to procedures rather than outcomes."Get rid of the jerks," he said referring to managers who prioritize procedure over results. "They admire a problem," he added. "I say they're like good bureaucrats. They like the process, not the outcome. Whereas I like the outcome."Continuing further, Jamie Dimon shared that one of the signs of bureaucracy in a company i when employees withhold information or create unnecessary delays. "If [information] isn't shared properly, I generally just cancel the meeting," Dimon said at the conference.He then talked about JP Morgan where he revealed meeting materials are distributed in advance to ensure participants have access to the same information before discussions begin. This is to ensure that the information is not withheld and creates needless friction within organizations.Dimon stated that he prefers small teams over large committee structures. "Get the people in the room and work it out," he said. "Don't allow it to go back and forth with groups for six months or nine months or a year."
Article Summary: JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon warned that bureaucracy can quietly undermine organizations from within. Dimon: "Bureaucracy, complacency and arrogance will take down a company" He said the solution should start with management accountability and removing leaders who become too attached to procedures.

Article Title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison believes America is on right track with AI, he sees robots taking jobs, and says what is needed is right taxation system
Article Text:
“We need to change from taxing human labour to taxing value added,”

“So when the robots add value, all that value that the robots add is taxed, and we could have

universal high income

.”

How robots could reduce costs while replacing some jobs

“kind of nonsensical”

How would universal high income work

“reverse income tax”

Larry Ellison believes AI can make everyone wealthier. The Oracle co-founder and chief technology officer says robots will take over some jobs, but argues that greater productivity and changes to taxation could help spread the resulting wealth. Speaking at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas, he described a future in which automation reduces the cost of goods and services while US governments collect revenue from the value machines create.he said.His argument links AI’s economic benefits to how governments distribute them, with less reliance on taxing people’s work.Ellison rejected the suggestion that AI would eventually replace everyone, calling that prediction. However, he acknowledged that automation would displace some workers, pointing to rideshare services as an example.He argued that better tools could also allow people to accomplish more. In the supplied account of his remarks, he cited robotic surgeons and aircraft autopilot systems to illustrate how technology can change work and improve productivity.To explain the potential effect on prices, Ellison described a hypothetical house built entirely by robots. If human labour previously accounted for 80% of its cost, he suggested, automating construction could substantially reduce that expense.The example illustrated his prediction about cheaper production; it was not a reported result from an actual housing project.Ellison’s proposal centres on taxing the economic value generated by automation and using that revenue to support people’s incomes. Universal basic income generally means regular payments intended to cover essential living costs. The universal high income he described would go further, relying on AI-driven productivity to support higher living standards even as machines do more of the work.He also referred to economist Milton Friedman’s negative income tax proposal, describing it as a. Broadly, such a system pays people whose incomes fall below a specified threshold. Ellison’s comments outlined a possible direction for taxation rather than a detailed policy. The supplied excerpts do not specify tax rates, payment amounts, or eligibility rules.He acknowledged that the transition would take more than a decade, with robots gradually taking on more tasks people don't want to do.
Article Summary: Larry Ellison believes AI can make everyone wealthier. Oracle co-founder and chief technology officer says robots will take over some jobs, but argues that greater productivity and changes to taxation could help spread the resulting wealth. Article Title: As IPO nears, Claude-maker Anthropic is set to make hundreds of employees millionaires; and it is worrying CEO Dario Amodei, making HR ask new hires: If ...
Article Text:
IPO could create a new class of AI millionaires

The interview question

Dario Amodei's concern: Mission over money

The talent war

Wealth concentration worries AI leaders

As AI giant Anthropic moves closer to a blockbuster initial public offering that could value the company between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion, the Claude-maker is poised to create a new wave of wealthy tech employees. But while the potential windfall could mint hundreds of employee millionaires, it is also creating an unusual concern for CEO Dario Amodei, according to a report by Fortune. The company is reportedly asking prospective employees during culture interviews how they would react if Anthropic abandoned its AI ambitions for safety reasons and the company's stock subsequently fell to zero. The unusual question is designed to gauge whether candidates are motivated primarily by the company's mission or by the prospect of financial gains from a future IPO. According to a report cited by Fortune, one candidate said they told interviewers they would not be happy if the stock became worthless, but would want to balance ethical goals with building a sustainable business.Anthropic is targeting a November IPO that could value the company as high as $2 trillion, potentially surpassing the record-setting public debut of SpaceX, Fortune reported. With more than 2,500 employees and stock-based compensation widely used across the company, such a valuation could generate massive wealth for current staff.The prospect of hundreds of employees becoming millionaires appears to be raising concerns among company leaders, particularly as Anthropic attempts to maintain its identity as an AI safety-focused organisation rather than a traditional high-growth technology company.Anthropic is reportedly asking job candidates in culture interviews how they would feel if the company someday dropped its AI ambitions for safety reasons and the decision sent its stock to zero, according to Axios. One candidate who described the process on the anonymous workplace site Blind said they were honest and would not be happy if the stock went to zero, adding that they would want to combine doing the most good and staying ethical with building a sustainable business.CEO Dario Amodei, whose net worth is estimated at $13.6 billion, has reportedly expressed concern about how the company’s huge financial incentives could affect its ability to retain employees who are truly committed to its mission. Anthropic is a public benefit corporation and has long tried to set itself apart from rivals such as OpenAI by focusing on AI safety and the long-term benefit of humanity. Its values statement says the mission is what everyone is there for.Anthropic has long distinguished itself from rivals by emphasising AI safety and what it describes as the "long-term benefit of humanity." As a public benefit corporation, the company's mission plays a central role in its culture and decision-making. Fortune reports that Amodei, whose own estimated net worth stands at roughly $13.6 billion, has expressed concerns that enormous financial incentives could make it harder to identify and retain employees who genuinely believe in the company's mission. The firm's values statement emphasises that its mission should be the guiding force behind decisions rather than competing financial motivations.The reported interview question reflects that concern by asking candidates to consider a scenario where the company prioritises safety over commercial success, even if doing so destroys shareholder value.Anthropic is competing with Meta, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI for top researchers and engineers. In its S-1 filing, dated October 26, the company acknowledged that hiring and retaining qualified staff on competitive terms has become exceptionally difficult and has intensified significantly, particularly in the San Francisco Bay Area, where it is headquartered.Fortune says Anthropic is currently offering base salaries of $350,000 to $850,000 for staff software engineering roles. It has more than 600 open positions, including about 120 in sales, more than 60 in AI research and engineering, and 50 in security. Some candidates are reportedly spending more than $4,000 on private coaching to improve their chances, and Aline Lerner, founder of the prep company Interviewing.io, told Bloomberg that the maths works when a few thousand dollars can raise a salary by $200,000.The potential wealth creation at Anthropic comes amid broader concerns about the economic impact of the AI boom. Amodei has previously warned that artificial intelligence could concentrate wealth among a relatively small group of people if safeguards are not put in place. Earlier this year, Amodei and Anthropic's six other co-founders, including his sister Daniela Amodei, committed to giving away 80% of their wealth. In a public letter, Amodei argued that excessive wealth concentration could "break society" and said wealthy individuals have a responsibility to help address inequality that may be worsened by AI.As Anthropic prepares for what could be one of the largest public offerings in technology history, the company finds itself balancing two competing realities: attracting top talent with lucrative pay packages and stock grants, while ensuring employees remain committed to the safety-focused mission that has defined the company since its founding.
Article Summary: Anthropic is reportedly asking job candidates in culture interviews how they would feel if the company abandoned its AI ambitions for safety reasons. The unusual question is designed to gauge whether candidates are motivated primarily by the company's mission or by the prospect of financial gains from a future IPO. CEO Dario Amodei has reportedly expressed concern about how the company’s huge financial incentives could affect its ability to retain employees who are truly committed to its mission.

Article Title: Apple HomeView's built-in camera may gain recording and motion detection features
Article Text:
Apple's Next HomeView Could Swivel a 9-Inch Screen on a Robotic Arm to Face You

Hidden code points to security camera mode

HomeView already includes a built-in camera

Privacy-focused features reportedly in development

Apple yet to confirm feature

Apple’s new HomeView smart display may be able to act as a home security camera, according to references found in its software, The Verge reports. A Reddit user spotted the feature in the settings files of HomeView Software 27.2. Apple has not announced anything about it, and Digital Trends notes that the feature is not active in the current software.The HomeView is Apple’s recently unveiled smart home display. It already has a built-in camera for FaceTime calls and facial recognition. The camera is a 12MP unit that can recognise people on sight, which matters in a home shared by a whole family. The settings files suggest Apple could also use the same hardware for motion detection, live streaming and video recording through HomeKit Secure Video.According to a report by The Verge, Reddit user "pdfu" uncovered references within HomeView software version 27.2 that describe a dedicated security camera mode. The code strings mention motion detection, live streaming, video recording options, and several privacy-focused features. One setup screen reportedly states: "Your HomeView can be used as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video." The discovery suggests that Apple may be planning to leverage the HomeView's built-in camera for home monitoring purposes, although the company has not officially announced such a feature.Apple unveiled the HomeView smart display at its "Welcome Home" event in October 2026. The device features a 7-inch display and a 12-megapixel camera designed for FaceTime calls and facial recognition. The camera can recognise multiple users and personalise content based on who is standing in front of the device. The HomeView currently serves as a central smart home control hub, allowing users to manage connected devices, view feeds from security cameras and access Siri-powered smart home features.The leaked code strings indicate that Apple is building several privacy protections into the potential security camera mode. According to the report, video feeds would only be viewable by members of the household, while the device would display a visual indicator and play a sound whenever someone starts watching the camera feed or when recording begins. Household members would also reportedly receive notifications whenever security camera settings are changed. The software code further points to configurable settings that would allow users to determine what the camera should detect, stream or record depending on whether they are at home, away or asleep.While the code references strongly hint at upcoming functionality, Apple has not publicly confirmed plans to turn HomeView into a security camera. The Verge noted that the company may still be refining privacy safeguards before rolling out such a feature, given Apple's longstanding emphasis on user privacy and security. If introduced, the feature would further expand HomeView's role within Apple's growing smart home ecosystem and could make the device a more direct competitor to smart displays from rivals that already offer integrated home monitoring capabilities.
Article Summary: Hidden code points to security camera mode on Apple's HomeView smart display. HomeView already includes a built-in camera for FaceTime calls and facial recognition. Code strings mention motion detection, live streaming, video recording options, and several privacy-focused features. Apple yet to confirm feature.

Article Title: Google is building a robot doctor for NASA, as Artemis mission advances from Moon to Mars, and says it will help astronauts to handle ...
Article Text:
Here's the complete post by Google's Jim Kelly

Optimizing crew time and safety

Adapting spatial awareness and vision-language-action models for robotic systems

Space: the ultimate edge-computing environment

Pioneering the future of crew safety and space exploration

Google and NASA are collaborating to develop an autonomous robotic medical assistant designed to support astronauts facing health emergencies and manage routine operational tasks during future deep-space expeditions. According to Google, the tie-up comes as, "NASA advances its Artemis program to send astronauts on increasingly difficult missions to explore more of the Moon, build a sustained human presence there with a Moon Base, and build on their foundation for the first crewed missions to Mars."The initiative aims to address a critical hurdle for long-duration spaceflight: Providing advanced healthcare when distance renders real-time communication with Earth impossible. When not handling medical duties alongside onboard crew, the dual-purpose system is envisioned to take on routine operational workloads, including hardware maintenance, equipment transport, and inventory management.The effort convenes specialists across multiple organizations, including Google Cloud, NASA’s Human Research Program, the robotics division at Johnson Space Center, and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory.The system builds directly upon the Crew Medical Officer Digital Assistant, an artificial intelligence platform Google and NASA began evaluating in 2025. That project focuses on enabling crews to independently diagnose and manage medical issues when signal delays prevent rapid consultations with terrestrial flight surgeons.“An astronaut on a future deep space mission to Mars could face severe operational challenges, including round-trip communication latencies of up to 44 minutes,” said Jim Kelly, vice president of Google’s public sector division. Presently, the project remains in an experimental phase. Current laboratory testing is focused on validating foundational robotic manipulation and general utility tasks, with project engineers noting that fully autonomous medical intervention in microgravity remains a long-term development goal.As NASA advances its Artemis program to send astronauts on increasingly difficult missions to explore more of the Moon, build a sustained human presence there with a Moon Base, and build on their foundation for the first crewed missions to Mars, crew safety and Earth-independent autonomy are paramount. An astronaut on a future deep space mission to Mars could face severe operational challenges—including round-trip communication latencies of up to 44 minutes, making real-time medical guidance for crew nearly impossible.Last year, Google Public Sector shared progress on the development of the Crew Medical Officer Digital Assistant (CMO-DA) - an automated Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) designed to assist astronauts with real-time medical guidance in remote and isolated environments. Today, we are building on this innovation with the development of a proof-of-concept physical, robotic system that aims to support deep space missions and could assist astronauts during NASA missions.The future Moon Base in the lunar South Pole region of the Moon is planned to support sustained human presence. Because every minute in space is a strictly limited resource, reducing the physical burden on astronauts to maximize their time for science and discovery is a top priority. To potentially address this challenge, NASA’s Human Research Program, Johnson Space Center Robotics Team, and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) collaborated with Google Public Sector to develop a robotic system. By handling routine logistics, this system could free up astronauts to focus on what humans do best: complex science and discovery.To maximize its utility for a lean crew, the robotic system is designed as a versatile "payload" handler capable of managing cargo, logistics, and equipment. When not needed for routine maintenance like organizing tools or securing compartments, it can pivot to medical support. For example, if an astronaut experiences severe back pain—a potential symptom of kidney stones—the robot could retrieve and prepare an ultrasound machine. This enables the human crew medical officer to focus entirely on analyzing the scan and treating the patient.Operating safely alongside humans in confined spacecraft is a complex challenge. Unlike factory robots in fixed, human-free environments, space systems utilizing Super Intelligence (SI) require flexible, human-directed tools to safely adapt to close quarters. Because they must also rely on limited sensory input like cameras, JPL is adapting satellite situational awareness intelligence tools—originally designed to track objects in orbit—to help the robotic system navigate and understand its 3D surroundings.To test this safely at Johnson Space Center’s iMETRO facility, Google DeepMind’s MuJoCo simulator was used, which is an advanced physics engine that allows the SI to practice complex movements in a highly accurate virtual environment before touching real hardware. In a recent proof-of-concept technology demonstration, the robotic system was tasked with a complex "pick-and-place" maneuver to locate and move a medical bag. By implementing an "eye-to-hand" camera configuration for enhanced spatial awareness, the open-source Pi0 model—developed by Physical Intelligence on Google Cloud infrastructure— achieved an initial 85% baseline success rate in these early lab environments, providing a strong foundation for the next phase of rigorous training and safety refinement. Because vision-language-action (VLA) models connect language directly to physical movement, astronauts could direct the robotic system flexibly via standard English text prompts.Processing these complex tasks requires significant computing power, which presents another hurdle: space is the ultimate edge computing environment. Spacecraft cannot rely on continuous connections to Earth-based data centers. To solve this, the Google team harnessed Google Cloud G4 instances to rapidly train the underlying models, fine-tuning the 4-billion parameter Pi0 model in just 2.5 hours. Crucially, they demonstrated that the fine-tuned models can then operate locally on compact, energy-efficient edge devices. Over the last two years, the team tested approximately 15 different edge computing devices to find ones that run efficiently on lightweight, low-power hardware required for future Mars missions.Looking ahead, the ultimate goal is to build a robotic system that can execute a variety of tasks via simple voice instructions, under the astronauts’ direct supervision and command. For instance, the robot might be directed to assist with routine health monitoring—such as capturing basic vitals or simple ultrasounds—under the strict guidance of a human crew medical officer. This ensures astronauts receive the physical assistance they might not be able to perform by themselves, without ever replacing human decision-making.This collaboration between Google Public Sector and NASA can help pave the way for increasingly difficult missions that push the bounds of scientific discovery.
Article Summary: Google and NASA are collaborating to develop an autonomous robotic medical assistant to support astronauts facing health emergencies and manage routine operational tasks during future deep-space expeditions. The initiative aims to address a critical hurdle for long-duration spaceflight: Providing advanced healthcare when distance renders real-time communication impossible.
